_doc: Which crew pre_tool_call hooks, krew plugins, crew skills and hermes cron jobs each profile runs: the reference install's placement, read by crew/scripts/krew-crew-install.py (--profiles writes the hooks block into each profile's config.yaml and copies each profile's skills; plugins are enabled by krew-install init; --crons creates the cron jobs). A hook with `path` runs that file under $KREW_HOME directly (the T0 gate: never behind a runner or an off switch); one with `script` runs crew/scripts/<script> through krew-crew-run. `fail_closed: true` is carried into the hook spec (a crashed or timed-out gate refuses the call; hermes shell hooks fail OPEN otherwise). Edit $KREW_HOME/crew/config/profile-kit.json to change it.

profiles._doc: Each crew profile's config as the reference install runs it (2026-10-10): the Board class description (= profile.yaml description, what Ada's decomposer routes by; the SOUL carries the same class line), toolsets (cli adds `docs`; cron and api_server = toolsets), agent caps, delegation, memory, tool_search (eager/defer), terminal. krew_install_init.profile_config writes them into a fresh profile's config.yaml and profile.yaml; nothing you already have is overwritten. {{deliverables_dir}} / {{hermes_home}} / {{live_tree}} are filled from krew.yaml (deliverables_dir, live_tree) or dropped.

ada.description: Board orchestrator and sole kanban inbox. Decomposes, assigns, heartbeats; does not implement on the host. Risky or untrusted work: spin consultants in docker. Goal-mode is judged by Ada's crew goal_judge, not Vera.

vera.description: Board reviewer, and the ONLY reviewer: every kanban_request_review comes to her on the same card; she approves it or sends it back with kanban_request_changes. Prodgate approve/reject, crystal and M&S verification, taste and architecture review; a render is judged with look_compare against its target. Builders build — do not send Vera the implement. Not the Goal-mode judge (Ada's crew goal_judge). Spawn-only.

lila.description: Designer and researcher, and the crew's only browser. Commissioned research and look-into cards, web and doc reading, specs and design.md, clip review and render minting through her tools (image_generate, video_generate, krew-render, render-lane), judged against the target with look_compare; glyph and delight research. No terminal: never a host implement, unit, or dependency card, and never a render job that needs a shell (ffmpeg, compositing, stitching, frame pinning, render-submit or pose scripts) — those are Bash's. Ada pins assignee=lila. Spawn-only — in-run adversarial subs, not Vera board review, not Goal.

steward.description: System architect of record, plus M&S and host security. Reads scout world/stack notes as data; bounded throwaway spikes only — never swap prod engines. Files the owner's reports in the deliverables folder ({{deliverables_dir}}) and archives by filename date into reports/ and kanban-archive/. Logs → kanban with resolution in that inbox. Coder 2 + default assignee: bounce undecomposed Ready one-liners to triage. Host terminal. Equal peer of Bash for dep, mitigation, and builds.

bash.description: Coder 1 — host-terminal implement, dep-review, mitigation, and builds, and every render job that needs a shell: ffmpeg compositing and stitching, frame pinning, render-submit and pose scripts, judged against the target with look_compare. Equal peer of Steward: split batches; never dump a whole batch on one coder. Adversarial-gate on non-trivial work. Not a dispatcher.

scout.description: Local-AI world and stack SOTA notes. Search + web + file into the owner inbox only. No host shell, no sudo, no kanban, no spikes. Steward is the architect of record and reads these notes as data.

judge.description: Judge — one call, one verb. Reads a card a detector already diagnosed (a worker that did the work and forgot the verb, an ownerless block) and answers with ONE `VERB:` line on the source card, then completes its own card. Never assign work here: only kanban-loop and the board gate file judge cards. No implement, no review, no research, no terminal.

zoey.description: Spoken assistant and Chief of Staff: front door, the Wall, and the owner's voice. Presence SoT only from the Wall's presence rail — never invent headcount. Rules the Decide queue, spot-checks the crew's deliverables and the improvement round, and reports her calls to the owner. Creates cards for Ada; not a card assignee — never route implement, research, or render work here.
zoey._doc: the front door: see docs/ZOEY-KIT.md; her toolsets are the hands belt, the full kit rides the hands child

tier0._doc: The T0 gate (rails/tier0_gate.py, policy $KREW_HOME/tier0.yaml), the same spec rails/krew_hooks.py writes; profile-kit lists it so the kit is one list. Zoey's rules in the policy (route zoey-kit): no terminal / execute_code / process, write_file / patch judged by a path BLOCK list; KREW_T0_MODE=enforce on the gateway.

zoey-tool-callout._doc: One short spoken line when a profile starts a tool (through the Wall's player /v1/announce; silent with no Wall or voice.json voice: off). The reference's matcher: `kanban_` on every crew profile, the long one on zoey (matcher_by_profile).

test-sandbox._doc: A pytest from a worker shell runs in its own HOME (the reference's test sandbox hook on the two coders and the reviewer); rails/krew_hooks.py writes the same spec.

hooks._doc: The reference order of a profile's pre_tool_call list is `_order` (close-clean first, the T0 gate before the sandbox, the callout, the count last).

plugins._doc: hindsight is the catalog plugin (vectorize-io/hindsight, pinned in crew/hindsight/plugin-pin.json; krew-install --memory installs it); the rest ship in plugins/.

skills._doc: Which crew skills each profile carries (the reference install's placement). krew-crew-install.py --profiles copies each into $HERMES_HOME/profiles/<profile>/skills/krew/<skill>; krew-kitting allows a krew skill on the profile that has it. Zoey carries seventeen (the reference install's profile skills folder, 2026-10-09). 2026-10-10: the seven crew profiles' rows are the reference profiles' skills folders; studio-only skills (mouth-place-and-shape, pose-flourish, viseme-bank-map, composer-coach, demo-rounds, hub-intake) stay with the studio.

crons._doc: hermes cron jobs that are a profile's own (a real schedule, not the window's placeholder): krew-crew-install.py --crons creates one that is missing (hermes -p <profile> cron create <schedule> <prompt> --name <name> --monitor-script <script>), copies the monitor script into $HERMES_HOME/profiles/<profile>/scripts/, and pins the prompt from the script's CRON_PROMPT (its install_cron_prompt) so the two never drift.

needs-zoey-watch._doc: Zoey's Decide watch: the monitor prints presence + the open escalation cards (stable bytes; beat= re-wakes her hourly while a software-rulable card waits); she rules every card, oldest first.

kanban-heartbeat.prompt: Check the kanban board and post a concise status update: any new blockers or decisions since the last beat. Keep it to ONE card. Do NOT record ephemeral data (tool raw output) to memory.
kanban-heartbeat._doc: Ada's hourly board beat (the reference's kanban-heartbeat cron). The other crew crons carry the placeholder schedule and are fired by the window (crew-crons.json).
kanban-heartbeat._paused_why: Created paused on a fresh install: an hourly card is a card generator. hermes -p ada cron resume kanban-heartbeat starts it (README, Card generators).
